mainTopic: The second מזבח's size and location, and which features of the מזבח are required
overview: This amud opens with the last words of a ברייתא: the מזבח may not be built over tunnels. Next, רב יוסף explains why the מזבח of the second בית המקדש was bigger. In the end he says that the builders found a פסוק comparing the מזבח to the sixty-אמה בית. Three אמוראים then explain how the builders knew the exact spot of the מזבח. רבי יוחנן and a ברייתא add that three נביאים came back from the גולה to guide them. A new ברייתא teaches that the קרן, כבש, יסוד and square shape are required, but the exact measurements are not. רב הונא learns this from the word "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ", which leads to a discussion of the כרכוב, and רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that there were two of them. Finally, רבי מני says the מזבח may not be smaller than משה's. רב יוסף's answer of "one אמה" is explained by אביי as the space left for the wood pile, and רב יוסף begins answering his mockers on the next amud.

steps.title: The altar may not be built over tunnels
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a ברייתא: the מזבח may not be built on top of hollow tunnels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not build it on top of tunnels.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a ברייתא that started on the previous page. It adds one more rule: the מזבח cannot sit over hollow tunnels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is listing what the ground under the מזבח must be like. This last rule tells us the מזבח has to rest on solid ground, not on hollow spaces underneath.

keyTerms.meaning: Tunnels or hollow spaces under the ground
On top of

phrases.english: And not on top of tunnels.
phrases.notes: This finishes a list that started on the previous page. The 'it' being built is the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מְחִילּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from the previous page about how the מזבח must be built.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח may not be built over hollow tunnels.

steps.title: רב יוסף: only the second altar reached full size
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests that a ברייתא on the פסוק in עזרא supports this idea: the second מזבח finally reached its proper full size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Isn't this what was taught in a ברייתא? 'And they set the altar upon its bases' means that they reached its full measurements.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is explaining why the second מזבח was bigger. He brings a ברייתא that reads a פסוק in עזרא as saying the builders of the second בית המקדש finally reached the מזבח's full size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on its bases' are read as 'at its true, proper size.' If so, the second מזבח was the ideal one, and the first מזבח was smaller than it should have been. That is exactly the claim the גמרא will attack next.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this what was taught in a ברייתא?
Its base, its proper set place
Its measurements

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Isn't this what was taught in a ברייתא:
"And they set the altar upon its bases"
phrases.notes: עזרא ג:ג

phrases.english: meaning that they reached its full measurements?
phrases.notes: In other words, only in the second בית המקדש did the מזבח reach its proper size.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to explaining why the second מזבח was larger.
steps.raayaObject: The second מזבח was the one built at the proper full size.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the words 'עַל מְכוֹנָתוֹ' in עזרא ג:ג.

steps.title: But the first Temple was built from God's own plan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the first בית המקדש was built from a written plan given by ה׳, so its מזבח could not have been too small.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'All this in writing, from the hand of ה׳, He made me understand'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's idea. דוד said the whole plan of the first בית המקדש came in writing from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ה׳ gave the plan, the first מזבח was exactly the right size. So you cannot say that only the second מזבח reached the proper measurements.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
In writing
He made me understand

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the second מזבח was wrong. It only rejects the claim that the first מזבח was missing its proper size.

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "All this in writing,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א כח:יט. דוד is describing the plan he gave שלמה for building the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: from the hand of ה׳ upon me, He made me understand"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: ״הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב מִיַּד ה׳ עָלַי הִשְׂכִּיל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's reading from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only the second מזבח reached its proper size.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first בית המקדש followed a plan from ה׳, so its מזבח must already have been the right size.

steps.title: רב יוסף's new answer: a verse allowed enlarging the altar to sixty cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף drops his first idea. The builders of the second בית המקדש found a פסוק that compares the מזבח to the בית, so the מזבח may be as large as sixty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: They found a verse and interpreted it: 'And דוד said: This is the house of ה׳ God, and this is the altar for burnt offerings for Israel.' The altar is like the house. Just as the house is sixty cubits, so too the altar may be sixty cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new explanation. The first מזבח was fine, but the builders of the second one used a פסוק to make it bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'house' and 'altar' side by side, so they are compared. The בית was sixty אמות, so the מזבח may also reach sixty אמות. This way the first מזבח was correct, and the second bigger one was also allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea and starts a new one)
He found a פסוק and expounded it
Just as ... so too (a comparison)
Cubit, a measure of length

steps.whatToRemember: The first מזבח was the proper size, as ה׳'s plan required. The second מזבח was enlarged because of a פסוק that compares the מזבח to the sixty-אמה בית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects the perfection of the first בית המקדש and still justifies the bigger מזבח of the second one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
He found a verse and expounded it:
phrases.notes: 'He' here means the builders of the second בית המקדש, who found this פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִיד: זֶה הוּא בֵּית ה׳ הָאֱלֹהִים,
phrases.english: "And David said: This is the house of ה׳ God,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א כב:א

phrases.english: and this is the altar for burnt offerings for Israel"
the altar is like the house;
just as the house is sixty cubits,
so too the altar may be sixty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: קְרָא אַשְׁכַּח וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's first idea after the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the explanation with a new derivation from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second מזבח was bigger because the first one fell short of the proper size.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first מזבח was perfect. The second was enlarged based on a פסוק comparing the מזבח to the sixty-אמה בית.

steps.title: How did they know where the altar stood?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: the builders could see where the old building had stood, but how did they know the exact spot of the מזבח?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for the house, its shape could be recognized. But the altar, how did they know where it was?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about building the second בית המקדש. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old building left clear marks, so its outline was easy to see. The מזבח has a very exact required spot, and nothing obvious showed where it had stood. The גמרא wants to know how the builders found it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense regarding...
It is recognizable
Its shape or outline
From where did they know?

phrases.english: Granted, regarding the house,
its shape is recognizable;
but regarding the altar,
how did they know?
phrases.notes: He means: how did they know the exact spot where the מזבח had stood.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בַּיִת – מִינַּכְרָא צוּרָתוֹ; אֶלָּא מִזְבֵּחַ – מְנָא יָדְעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size of the מזבח to how its location was identified in the second בית המקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the builders of the second בית המקדש identified the exact location of the מזבח.

steps.title: Three signs that showed them the spot of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, רבי יצחק נפחא, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני each explain how the builders found the exact place of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: They saw a built מזבח, with מיכאל the great angel standing and bringing קרבנות on it. רבי יצחק נפחא said: They saw the ashes of יצחק lying in that place. רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: Everywhere else in the בית they smelled קטורת, but from that one spot they smelled burning limbs of קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. Three אמוראים each describe a different sign that showed the builders exactly where the מזבח had stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The builders could see the outline of the old building, but the מזבח's spot needed a special sign. Each answer gives a different kind of sign: a vision of an angel, a vision of יצחק's ashes, or a smell that came from only one place. These are three separate opinions, not one story.

keyTerms.meaning: מיכאל, the great angel (literally 'the great prince')
The ashes of יצחק, connected to עקדת יצחק on this spot
The incense offered in the בית המקדש
Limbs of קרבנות burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the three answers together. Each אמורא gives his own separate sign; they are not three parts of one event.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
They saw an altar already built,
phrases.notes: "They" means the people building the second בית המקדש. He means they saw it in a vision.

phrases.english: and Michael, the great prince,
standing and offering on it.
And Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:
They saw the ashes of Yitzchak,
which were lying in that place.
And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
From the whole entire House
they smelled the smell of incense,
but from there they smelled the smell of limbs.
phrases.notes: "There" is the one spot where the מזבח belonged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: רָאוּ מִזְבֵּחַ בָּנוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5 about how they knew the exact place of the מזבח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three opinions: a vision of a built מזבח with מיכאל offering on it; a vision of יצחק's ashes; or the smell of burning limbs coming from that one spot.

steps.title: Three prophets came up from exile, according to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says three נביאים came back with the people and guided them about the מזבח, its place, and bringing קרבנות without a בית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Three נביאים came up with them from the גולה. One told them about the מזבח, one told them about the place of the מזבח, and one told them that they may bring קרבנות even when there is no בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יוחנן that gives another way the builders knew what to do: נביאים told them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new source of knowledge: prophecy. It covers the size and shape of the מזבח and its exact place, which ties back to Steps 4–5. The third נביא adds a new הלכה: קרבנות may be brought on a proper מזבח even before the בית is rebuilt.

keyTerms.meaning: Prophets
The exile (here, בבל)
Testified, told them with authority
Even though there is no בית המקדש standing

steps.whyThisMatters: The third נביא's message teaches that the מזבח, not the building, is what allows קרבנות to be offered.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה נְבִיאִים עָלוּ עִמָּהֶם מִן הַגּוֹלָה –
phrases.english: Three prophets came up with them from the exile:
one who testified to them about the altar,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד שֶׁהֵעִיד לָהֶם עַל מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: and one who testified to them about the place of the altar,
and one who testified to them that we offer sacrifices
even though there is no House.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation, prophecy, for how the builders knew about the מזבח and its place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three נביאים guided the returning people: about the מזבח, about its place, and that קרבנות may be offered without a בית.

steps.title: A different list of the three prophets
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב also counts three נביאים, but joins the מזבח and its place into one and adds a נביא about writing the תורה in כתב אשורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says three נביאים came up with them from the גולה. One told them about the מזבח and its place, one told them that they may bring קרבנות even when there is no בית, and one told them that the תורה should be written in כתב אשורית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a slightly different list of the three נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one נביא covers both the מזבח and its place, which leaves room for a third topic. That third נביא taught that the תורה should be written in כתב אשורית, the script we use today. The basic idea of three guiding נביאים stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
כתב אשורית, the square script used for a ספר תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Both lists have three נביאים, but they are not the same three topics. רבי יוחנן counts the מזבח and its place separately. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב joins them and adds the script of the תורה.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה נְבִיאִים עָלוּ עִמָּהֶן מִן הַגּוֹלָה –
phrases.english: Three prophets came up with them from the exile:
one who testified to them about the altar
and about the place of the altar,
and one who testified to them that we offer sacrifices
even though there is no House,
and one who testified to them about the Torah:
that it should be written in Ashurit script.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel version of רבי יוחנן's list with a different set of three topics.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three נביאים: one about the מזבח and its place, one about offering without a בית, and one about writing the תורה in כתב אשורית.

steps.title: Which parts of the altar are required
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: the קרן, כבש, יסוד, and square shape are required for the מזבח to be valid, but its length, width, and height are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The קרן, the כבש, the יסוד, and the square shape are required. The measure of its length, the measure of its width, and the measure of its height are not required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about which features a מזבח must have to be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some features are מעכבין: without them, the מזבח is not valid. The exact measurements are not מעכבין, so a מזבח of a different size still works. This fits Step 4, where the second מזבח was built larger than the first.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised corner at each corner of the מזבח
The ramp the כהנים walked up
The base of the מזבח
Being square
Required; without them the מזבח is not valid

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the second בית המקדש could change the מזבח's size and still have a valid מזבח.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The corner, the ramp, the base, and being square are indispensable.
The measure of its length and the measure of its width
and the measure of its height are not indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קֶרֶן וְכֶבֶשׁ וִיסוֹד וְרִיבּוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about which features of the מזבח are required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרן, כבש, יסוד, and square shape are מעכבין. The length, width, and height are not.

steps.title: Where do we learn this from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source teaches that these four features are required. This sets up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule without a פסוק. The גמרא now wants to know why some features are required and others are not.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these things derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source showing that the קרן, כבש, יסוד, and square shape are required.

steps.title: The word "the altar" makes it required
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: wherever the תורה uses the word "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ" about a feature, that feature is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The פסוק says "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ". Wherever it says "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ", it means the detail is required.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question from Step 10 by pointing to the word "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ" in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about the four required features use the word "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ". רב הונא reads that word as a sign that the detail is necessary for the מזבח to be valid. The measurements don't have this sign, so they are not required.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it required, so that without it the מזבח is not valid

steps.whatToRemember: The מזבח's קרן, כבש, יסוד, and square shape are required because the פסוק says "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ" about them. Its measurements can change, which is how the second מזבח could be built larger.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The verse says "the altar";
phrases.notes: He means that in each פסוק about these four features, the word "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ" appears.

phrases.english: wherever "the altar" is said, it is to make it indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר קְרָא: הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ" in a פסוק shows that the detail is מעכב.

steps.title: Should the כרכוב also be required?
steps.stepSummary: If every feature tied to 'הַמִּזְבֵּחַ' is required, then the כרכוב should be required too, because the פסוק calls it 'כַּרְכֹּב הַמִּזְבֵּחַ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is true, then the engraving according to רבי, and the surrounding ledge according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, should also be required! The פסוק says 'under the כרכוב of the מזבח', and a ברייתא says רבי holds the כרכוב is the engraving, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it is the surrounding ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב הונא's rule. It points to a feature the פסוק also links to 'הַמִּזְבֵּחַ', the כרכוב, that was not on the ברייתא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said any feature written with the word 'הַמִּזְבֵּחַ' is required. The פסוק says 'כַּרְכֹּב הַמִּזְבֵּחַ', so by his rule the כרכוב should be required. Whether that means the כיור or the סובב depends on the מחלוקת between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, but either way it is missing from the ברייתא's list.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if that is so...': it introduces a challenge that pushes a rule to its logical end
A part of the מזבח mentioned in the פסוק; its exact identity is debated
An engraving or decoration on the מזבח (רבי's view of the כרכוב)
The ledge that runs around the middle of the מזבח (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view)
Required; without it the item is invalid

phrases.english: But now, if that is so,
the engraving, according to רבי,
and the surrounding ledge, according to רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה –
is it also true that it is required?!
As it is written:
"And you shall put it under the karkov
of the altar beneath,"
phrases.notes: שמות 27:5. Notice the word 'הַמִּזְבֵּחַ', which is exactly what רב הונא's rule looks for.

phrases.english: And it is taught: What is the karkov?
רבי says: This is the engraving.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: זֶה הַסּוֹבֵב!
phrases.english: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says: This is the surrounding ledge!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's rule from step 11 by applying it to the כרכוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that anything written with 'הַמִּזְבֵּחַ' is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כרכוב is also written with 'הַמִּזְבֵּחַ', yet the ברייתא in step 9 does not list it as required.

steps.title: Yes, the surrounding ledge is required too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge: yes, it is required. It proves this from a ברייתא where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds the סובב to the list of required parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is required. A ברייתא teaches: on that day a corner of the מזבח was damaged, and they sealed it with a lump of salt. They did not do this to make the מזבח fit for the service, only so the מזבח would not look damaged. That is because any מזבח without a corner, ramp, base, and square shape is invalid. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: the surrounding ledge is also required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not argue with the challenge. It agrees and brings a ברייתא showing that at least one תנא really counts the סובב as required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The salt only covered the damage so it would not look bad. It could not truly fix the קרן, so the מזבח stayed unfit. That shows a missing קרן invalidates the מזבח. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds the כרכוב is the סובב, adds the סובב to the list, which fits רב הונא's rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes; the גמרא accepts the point
Was damaged or chipped
A lump or fistful of salt
Damaged, blemished

steps.confusionAlert: The salt did NOT make the מזבח valid again. It was only so the מזבח would not look damaged. The מזבח stayed unfit for the service until it was properly fixed.

phrases.english: Yes;
as it is taught:
On that day the corner of the altar was damaged,
phrases.notes: 'That day' is when people threw אתרוגים at a צדוקי כהן; the story is in סוכה 48b.

phrases.english: and they brought a lump of salt and sealed it;
and not because that made it fit for the service,
but so that the altar would not be seen damaged.
For any altar that does not have
a corner, a ramp, a base, and a square shape – is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַסּוֹבֵב.
phrases.english: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says: Even the surrounding ledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין; דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by accepting it and backing it up from a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Acceptance of the challenge, supported by a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כרכוב seemed to break רב הונא's rule because it was not on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כרכוב really is required. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says so outright about the סובב.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule holds up: the כרכוב, written with 'הַמִּזְבֵּחַ', is also required, as רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says about the סובב.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines the כרכוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the כרכוב is the space between corner and corner, the cubit where the כהנים walked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: What is the כרכוב? Between one corner and the next corner, the walking place of the כהנים' feet, a cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives another definition of the כרכוב. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי (an engraving) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (the ledge), this ברייתא puts the כרכוב on top of the מזבח. The way it is worded seems to mix the space between the corners with the walkway of the כהנים, which the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the כהנים' feet walked
A cubit, a unit of measure

phrases.english: The Sages taught: What is the karkov?
Between corner and corner,
the place where the priests' feet walk, a cubit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ כַּרְכּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about what the כרכוב mentioned in step 12 actually is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כרכוב is a cubit-wide area on top of the מזבח, between the corners.

steps.title: Did the כהנים really walk between the corners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording: the כהנים did not walk in the space between the corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say the כהנים walked between one corner and the next?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא, which seems to say the walkway was the space between the corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the ברייתא makes the corner-to-corner area and the walkway one and the same. The גמרא finds that unlikely: the area between the corners is not where the כהנים walked.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say...?!': it introduces a question that sounds absurd
They would walk

phrases.english: Is that to say that the priests
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the one in square brackets; either way it means the same thing.

phrases.english: would walk between corner and corner?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כֹּהֲנִים בֵּין קֶרֶן לְקֶרֶן הֲווֹ אָזְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording, which makes the walkway the same as the area between the corners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהנים did not walk in the area between the corners, so the two cannot be the same place.

steps.title: Two separate cubits
steps.stepSummary: Fix the reading: the כרכוב is between the corners, AND there is a separate cubit where the כהנים walked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: and the place where the כהנים' feet walked was another cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read the ברייתא. It adds the word 'and', so the walkway becomes a separate area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'and' added, the ברייתא lists two different cubits: the כרכוב cubit between the corners, and a separate cubit for walking. That removes the problem raised in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say...': it introduces a corrected reading

phrases.english: Rather, say:
and the place where the priests' feet walk – a cubit.
phrases.notes: The key change is the little word 'and' at the start. It makes the walkway its own cubit, separate from the כרכוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by changing how the ברייתא is read.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The walkway and the area between the corners were the same place.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two separate cubits on top of the מזבח.

steps.title: A פסוק puts the כרכוב halfway down
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק places the net 'under its כרכוב, beneath, up to its halfway point', which suggests the כרכוב is on the side of the מזבח, not on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'under its כרכוב beneath, up to its halfway point'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that the כרכוב is on top of the מזבח, using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the כרכוב to the middle height of the מזבח. That fits a feature on the side of the מזבח, not a strip on top as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it written...?': it introduces a challenge from a פסוק
Its halfway point

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"Under its karkov beneath, up to its halfway point"!
phrases.notes: שמות 38:4

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: תַּחַת כַּרְכֻּבּוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה עַד חֶצְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the location of the כרכוב given in steps 14 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the כרכוב is on top of the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק connects the כרכוב to the halfway point of the מזבח, so it should be on the side.

steps.title: There were two כרכובים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק: there were two כרכובים, one for beauty and one to keep the כהנים from slipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: There were two. One was for beauty, and one was for the כהנים so they would not slip.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק settles the conflict between the ברייתא and the פסוק by saying there were two different things called כרכוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's כרכוב, at the halfway point, was decorative. The ברייתא's כרכוב, on top, was a safety feature so the כהנים would not slip. Each source is talking about a different one, so they do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: There were two
For beauty, decoration
Slip

steps.whatToRemember: There were two כרכובים: a decorative one halfway up the מזבח (the פסוק's) and a safety one on top for the כהנים (the ברייתא's).

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
There were two;
one for beauty,
and one for the priests, so that they would not slip.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תְּרֵי הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different things (each source is talking about a different כרכוב)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one כרכוב, so the פסוק and the ברייתא clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were two כרכובים: a decorative one at the middle height and a safety one on top.

steps.title: The altar's exact measurements are not required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא: the exact length, width, and height of the מזבח do not block its validity.
steps.simpleTranslation: The length, width, and height measurements of the מזבח are not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line from the ברייתא quoted earlier. If the מזבח is not built to the exact measurements, it is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed the parts of the מזבח, like the כרכוב. Now the focus moves to its overall size. The rule is that these measurements do not invalidate the מזבח, and the next step will add a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Measurement
Height
They do not hold back, meaning they are not required for validity

phrases.english: The measurement of its length and the measurement of its width
phrases.notes: "Its" means the מזבח's. This line is from the ברייתא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: and the measurement of its height are not indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדַּת אׇרְכּוֹ וּמִדַּת רׇחְבּוֹ וּמִדַּת קוֹמָתוֹ אֵין מְעַכְּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כרכוב discussion back to another line of the ברייתא, about the מזבח's overall size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח's length, width, and height measurements do not invalidate it.

steps.title: רבי מני: not smaller than משה's altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני limits the rule: the מזבח may not be made smaller than the one משה built.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני says: as long as it is not smaller than the מזבח that משה made.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני puts a limit on the rule from step 19. The size can vary, but only down to a minimum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measurements are flexible, but they have a floor. משה's מזבח sets the smallest size allowed. This raises the obvious question of how big משה's מזבח was.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that, on condition that
He makes it smaller
The מזבח that משה built in the מדבר

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani says:
provided that one does not decrease it
below the altar that Moses made.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִפְחָתֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a minimum size to the flexible-measurement rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח may not be smaller than משה's מזבח.

steps.title: How big was משה's altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the minimum size is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step: how large is the minimum set by משה's מזבח?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מני set a minimum but did not give a number. The גמרא wants the actual measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how big is the minimum, the size of משה's מזבח?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the number behind רבי מני's minimum.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the minimum, משה's מזבח.

steps.title: רב יוסף: one cubit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the minimum is one אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: one אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a number for the minimum: one אמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer sounds surprisingly small. That is why the next step pushes back on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of length

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: One cubit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.

steps.title: They laughed: the verse says five by five
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש mocks רב יוסף, because the פסוק says משה's מזבח was five אמות by five אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at him: the פסוק says, "Five אמות long and five אמות wide, the מזבח shall be square."
steps.whatsHappening: The people in the בית מדרש challenge רב יוסף by quoting the פסוק. משה's מזבח was clearly five by five, not one אמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An explicit פסוק gives משה's מזבח a size of five אמות square. If that is the minimum, how can רב יוסף say one אמה? The challenge seems to make his answer impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed at him
Square

phrases.english: They mocked him:
"Five cubits long and five cubits wide;
phrases.notes: שמות 27:1

phrases.english: the altar shall be square"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחֲכוּ עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer using a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that משה's מזבח was one אמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly says five by five, so one אמה contradicts it.

steps.title: אביי: he meant the space for the wood pile
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that רב יוסף meant only the area for the מערכה, the wood pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: maybe the Master was talking about the place of the wood pile?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב יוסף. He suggests that one אמה refers to the space left for the wood pile, not the whole מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Start with five אמות. Take off one אמה on each side for the corners and one אמה on each side for the כהנים's walking path. That leaves exactly one אמה in the middle for the wood. This ties back to steps 14 through 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
The place of the wood pile on the מזבח
Master, a respectful way of saying "you"

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying משה's מזבח was only one אמה in total. The one אמה is only the inner area left for the fire after the corners and the walking path.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps the Master is speaking of the place of the arrangement of wood?
phrases.notes: Five minus a corner and a walking path on each side leaves one אמה in the middle for the wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי דִּלְמָא מְקוֹם מַעֲרָכָה קָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mockery by reinterpreting רב יוסף's one אמה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of what was being measured
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף meant the whole מזבח was one אמה, which contradicts the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant the inner wood area, which is one אמה after subtracting the corners and walking paths.

steps.title: רב יוסף confirms and turns to his mockers
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף confirms that אביי understood him correctly, and then applies a פסוק to those who mocked him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the Master, who is a great man, knows what I am saying. He applied to them:
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף agrees that אביי's explanation is what he meant. The final words set up a פסוק he will apply to the mockers, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the challenge: one אמה refers to the wood area. רב יוסף praises אביי for understanding him and is about to answer those who laughed.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man
He read about them, meaning he applied a פסוק to them

steps.whatToRemember: The מזבח's measurements are flexible, but it may not be smaller than משה's. רב יוסף's "one אמה" means the inner wood area of משה's five-by-five מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָר דְּגַבְרָא רַבָּה הוּא,
phrases.english: He said to him: The Master, who is a great man,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is speaking to אביי here.

phrases.english: knows what I am saying.
He read about them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people who mocked him. The פסוק he applies comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר דְּגַבְרָא רַבָּה הוּא יָדַע מַאי קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms אביי's explanation and sets up a פסוק aimed at the mockers.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף's one-אמה minimum refers to the wood area. He confirms this and turns to his critics.
